entries.name: HEAD
entries.means: the commit you have checked out — normally via the branch you're on

entries.name: @ — short for HEAD
entries.means: exactly the same thing as HEAD, two fewer keystrokes

entries.name: tilde — one step back
entries.means: the first parent of <rev>. HEAD~ is the commit before HEAD

entries.name: tilde n — n steps back
entries.means: walk back 3 commits, always taking the first parent. HEAD~3 is three commits ago on this line of history

entries.name: caret — first parent
entries.means: the same as <rev>~ for an ordinary commit: its first parent

entries.name: caret n — the nth parent
entries.means: the second parent of a merge commit — the branch that was merged in. Only merge commits have one

entries.name: peel to the tree
entries.means: the tree object of that commit, rather than the commit itself. HEAD^{tree} is the root directory of your last commit

entries.name: peel to a commit
entries.means: follow tags until you reach an actual commit. Useful because an annotated tag is an object in its own right

entries.name: search messages
entries.means: the newest commit whose message contains that text. :/fix typo finds it without you looking up an id

entries.name: an abbreviated object id
entries.means: any unambiguous prefix of a full 40-character id — usually 7 characters is plenty

reflog.title: Naming where a ref used to be

entries.name: at brace n — the nth reflog entry
entries.means: where HEAD pointed one move ago. HEAD@{0} is now, HEAD@{1} is before your last command — the undo button's address

entries.name: a branch's own reflog
entries.means: where the branch main pointed two of its own movements ago. Each ref has a separate log, so main@{2} and HEAD@{2} usually differ

entries.name: the previous branch
entries.means: the branch you were on before this one — what `git checkout -` uses

entries.name: the upstream branch
entries.say: at brace you, or at upstream
entries.means: the remote-tracking branch your branch is set to compare against, usually origin/<same name>

entries.name: where a push would go
entries.means: the ref `git push` would update — the same as @{u} in ordinary setups, different under triangular workflows

entries.name: ORIG_HEAD
entries.means: where HEAD was before the last big move (reset, rebase, merge, pull). `git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD` undoes it

entries.name: two dots — in B but not A
entries.means: the commits reachable from B that aren't reachable from A. main..feature is 'my branch's own commits'

entries.name: three dots — in either but not both
entries.means: the symmetric difference: everything either side has that the other doesn't. With --left-right, git marks which side each commit came from

entries.name: caret prefix — exclude
entries.means: the long form of a range: include B, exclude A. Takes any number of each, unlike ..

entries.name: just that commit
entries.means: the commit and none of its ancestors — a range containing exactly one commit

entries.name: --first-parent
entries.means: when walking, only ever follow parent number one — the trunk's own story, without the commits merged into it

entries.name: a branch's full name
entries.means: what the branch 'main' is really called. Branches live under refs/heads/

entries.name: a tag's full name
entries.say: refs tags v one point oh
entries.means: tags live under refs/tags/ and, by convention, don't move

entries.name: a remote-tracking ref
entries.means: your local note of where origin's main was when you last fetched. Written origin/main for short

entries.name: refs/stash
entries.means: the ref pointing at your most recent stash. Its reflog holds the older ones — which is why a dropped stash is recoverable

refspecs.title: Refspecs — what maps to what over the wire

entries.name: a refspec
entries.means: push or fetch the ref on the left into the ref on the right. `git push origin main:main` is the explicit form of the everyday push

entries.name: leading plus — allow non-fast-forward
entries.means: update even if it isn't a fast-forward. This is what --force does, written into the refspec itself

entries.name: empty source — delete
entries.means: push nothing into that ref, which deletes it. `git push origin :old-branch` removes the remote branch

entries.name: the default fetch refspec
entries.means: every branch on the remote becomes a remote-tracking ref locally. This line in .git/config is why origin/* exists

entries.name: double dash — end of options
entries.means: everything after this is a path, not a revision. `git checkout -- file` means the file, even if a branch shares its name

entries.name: a file at a revision
entries.means: the blob for that path in that commit. `git show HEAD~2:src/app.py` prints the old version without checking anything out

entries.name: pathspec magic — exclude
entries.means: everything except this. `git log -- . ':(exclude)*.lock'` skips the noisy files

entries.name: 100644 — an ordinary file
entries.means: a regular, non-executable file. The commonest thing in any tree

entries.name: 100755 — an executable file
entries.means: a regular file with the executable bit set. The only permission git records

entries.name: 120000 — a symlink
entries.means: the 'file' content is the path it points at

entries.name: 040000 — a subdirectory
entries.means: the entry is another tree object

entries.name: 160000 — a submodule
entries.means: a 'gitlink': the entry names a commit in another repository rather than any content in this one
